job.theme: a story about a lost umbrella
job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

response.passage: Arjun stood at the bustling Dadar station, clutching his faded blue umbrella, a gift from his grandfather, Mr. Deshmukh. It was 4:15 PM on a humid Tuesday, and the monsoon clouds hung heavy over Mumbai. Arjun boarded the local train, distracted by a conversation with his friend, Rohan. As the train screeched into Thane, Arjun rushed out, leaving the umbrella on the seat. He only realized his loss when the sudden downpour began at 5:30 PM. He blamed the heavy crowd for his forgetfulness, as the rush of people pushing toward the exit had completely overwhelmed his senses. Meanwhile, his sister, Meera, was at the library in Pune, reading about how lost items often end up in the railway lost-and-found office. Arjun felt a deep sense of regret, realizing that his lack of focus, rather than the crowd, was the true reason he had left the umbrella behind. He decided to call the station master the next morning, hoping that someone had turned it in. He remembered that his grandfather always said that objects are merely anchors for memories, and losing one does not mean losing the memory itself.
response.summary: Arjun loses his grandfather's umbrella on a train due to his own distraction. He later reflects on his mistake and plans to contact the station authorities to recover it.
